blocks.x: Sell-through +8 points and hero-SKU availability +24% — assortment intelligence

A global fashion group: a Retail & Consumer Goods program run on the outcome-linked model with a blended Achala IT Solutions team. The name stays behind the NDA; the numbers are published with permission.
Size-curve buys guessed; end-of-season markdowns absorbed the error.
Hero-SKU shortages at flagship doors while slow doors overstocked. Counterfeits and grey market contested authenticity with no verification path.

Assortment intelligence models curves by door with demand-transfer logic feeding allocation; clienteling copilots surface client history to associates; and a Ledger product-birth-certificate network powers consumer authenticity verification for flagship lines.

blocks.x: The three things that made it hold

items: the data spine was certified once and reused everywhere, which is why the numbers held up under audit.
evaluation was an engineering artifact, not a slide: the models earned production by passing a set the client's reviewers recognized as their own.
the trust question was answered before the chain was chosen — which is why this one survived procurement.

blocks.x: If you are considering the same pattern

Two things from the global fashion group program generalize — the governance shape and the gate design. Everything else was estate-specific, and pretending otherwise is how programs waste their first quarter The engagement model here was build-transfer; the same pattern runs fixed-scope where the estate allows it.
Figures on this page are the client's, reproduced with permission. Method notes and measurement designs are available under NDA.
The next step is small and real: one working session on the same diagnostic, your data, and a written feasibility read you can circulate.
